items.title: Trump threatens to isolate Iran. Who are its trading partners?
items.description: A threat by US President Donald Trump to impose unprecedented economic warfare and isolation on Iran could have implications for countries that trade with it. Trump warned of economic consequences for any country that supports Iran. Here are some of Iran’s main trading partners in recent years: Pakistan For Pakistan, any US action against countries involved in trade or assistance to Iran could be a serious setback, analysts said, amid Pakistan-Iran commitments to expand bilateral trade to $10 billion. Following past sanctions on Iran, formal trade between the two countries had come to a halt until recently. However, informal trade has taken exports and imports from both sides to approximately $4bn, according to unofficial statistics. After the Islamabad interim agreement was signed in June, efforts were quickly made to expand trade cooperation. Pakistan and Iran have for years traded oil, wheat, rice, live stocks and medicines through informal channels. India India’s trade with Iran dropped sharply in 2020, when Washington pressed on with sanctions on Tehran. Two-way trade was cut by more than two-thirds to nearly $4.8bn in the fiscal year 2019-20, from $17bn in the previous year. Over the years, trade between India and Iran has fallen further, and stood at $1.63bn in the fiscal year 2025-26, according to data from India’s commerce ministry. Indian exports worth $1.3bn make for the bulk of this trade as New Delhi predominantly ships cereals, tea, coffee and spices to Iran. Officials in New Delhi have previously maintained that such exports continue on humanitarian grounds and should remain outside the scope of any sanctions. China China, the biggest buyer of Iranian oil, could face additional pressures from the US over its purchases if Trump follows through on his promise. Over the past decade, China has created a ring-fenced system of refiners that process mainly Iranian oil and do not have much US exposure. Iranian oil delivered to China has long been branded as Malaysian, and more recently Indonesian, and trades in a tight loop, is settled in Chinese currency and involves a chain of difficult-to-track intermediaries, say refinery sources and traders involved in the business. The US Treasury in April imposed sanctions on a Chinese independent refinery for buying billions of dollars worth of Iranian oil and warned Chinese banks of secondary sanctions if they facilitated trade of Iranian oil. “Sanctions and pressure will not solve the problem. China calls on all parties concerned to take responsible measures to resolve the issue through political and diplomatic means,” Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian told reporters in a briefing. Over 80 per cent of Iran’s shipped oil has been destined for China, as Chinese independent refiners take advantage of discounted US-sanctioned oil. Kpler estimates that China bought an average of 1.38m barrels per day of Iranian oil in 2025. United Arab Emirates The United Arab Emirates has historically been one of Iran’s most critical economic lifelines, and Dubai’s banks have long held substantial Iranian-linked deposits, much of them now immobilised under US sanctions. The UAE was among Iran’s largest trade partners before the war, providing 30pc of its imports worth an overall $21bn in 2024, according to the World Trade Organisation’s latest figures. It also accounted for 13pc of Iran’s exports in the same year, the data showed. Non-oil foreign trade between the two countries totalled $6.6 billion in 2024, according to UAE economy ministry data, with the vast majority of trade represented by re-exports. This week, the UAE suspended all financial and economic transactions with Iran until further notice, citing a military escalation by Tehran with a missile threat, refocusing the spotlight on fraught ties between the countries. Turkiye Turkiye and Iran maintain significant economic ties, with Turkiye importing Iranian natural gas and exporting manufactured goods to Iran. Turkiye has not signalled any willingness to curtail commerce with Iran, with bilateral trade standing at around $5-6bn annually, with Turkiye exporting to Iran around $3bn. Turkiye imports almost all its natural gas consumption and Iran is a notable source, providing 13pc of all gas imports. Iraq Iraq’s trade with Iran reached more than $10bn in 2025, according to official Iraqi trade figures, with the relationship largely driven by Iranian exports of food, consumer goods and other products to the Iraqi market. Trade declined in 2026 after the Iran war started , which increased regional security risks and led to intermittent disruptions along key border crossings, as well as higher transport costs, said Mohammed Karim, an Iraqi trade ministry official with knowledge of trade activities with Iran. These conditions, combined with broader supply chain disruptions affecting the movement of goods, reduced the volume and reliability of cross-border commerce although the countries remain important trading partners, said Karim. Energy is a key part of the relationship. Iraq pays Iran around $4bn to $5bn a year for natural gas, according to Iraqi energy officials, with the gas used to generate electricity. Two Iraqi energy officials said any new US sanctions on Iraq could create significant challenges for Baghdad in maintaining payments for Iranian energy while avoiding exposure to US sanctions, particularly given existing restrictions that have forced Iraq to use restricted accounts to settle payments. Oman Oman has long maintained cordial ties with Iran, dating back to before the 1979 Islamic revolution, with Muscat often acting as a mediator between Iran and other countries, including the US. The countries’ trade relationship has grown in recent years, with trade of goods totalling $1.5bn in 2025 and $345m in the first four months of this year, according to data from Oman’s National Centre for Statistics and Information. Armenia Iran accounted for $768m, or 3.6pc of neighbouring Armenia’s total trade turnover in 2025, according to official Armenian statistics. Armenia’s trade turnover with Iran reached $371.4m in the first half of 2026, marking an 8.4pc increase. Exports were recorded at $42.8m, a 6pc decrease, while imports amounted to $336.9m, a 12pc increase. Some 20pc of Armenia’s foreign trade passes through Iran. Armenia and Iran have a gas for electricity swap agreement, where Armenia uses gas supplied by Iran to make electricity, which is then sent back to Iran as well as being used domestically in Armenia. Azerbaijan Trade turnover between Azerbaijan and Iran rose 4.5pc in January-June 2026 compared with January-June 2025, to $312.6m from $299.1m, according to Azerbaijan’s State Customs Committee. Azerbaijan’s imports from Iran increased 1.5pc to $297m from $292.7m in the same period of 2025. Azerbaijan’s exports to Iran rose 2.4-fold to $15.6m from $6.4 million in January-June 2025. Iran accounted for 3.56pc of Azerbaijan’s total imports, up from 2.54pc in January-June 2025.

items.title: Un week-end de GTA VI en échange d'un contrat militaire : un bataillon américain offre des congés spéciaux pour retenir ses soldats
items.description: Au sein de l'armee americaine, des militaires se sont vu proposer des jours de conge supplementaires pour jouer a Grand Theft Auto VI des sa sortie, en echange de la reconduction de leur contrat, a rapporte CBS News le 19 août, citant des sources. Selon la chaîne americaine, le commandement militaire americain souhaitait proposer aux soldats une « incitation » correspondant a leurs centres d'interet. Cette initiative concerne environ 130 militaires eligibles a la reconduction de leur contrat. D'apres CBS News, cette « incitation » est en vigueur dans l'un des bataillons de Fort Stewart, dans l'etat de Georgie. Les militaires se sont vu proposer de prolonger leur contrat pour une duree de deux a six ans entre le 1er août et le 14 novembre, en echange d'un conge special de quatre jours a l'occasion de la sortie du jeu video le 19 novembre. Selon la chaîne, vingt soldats ont deja profite de cette offre. L'armee americaine utilise depuis plusieurs annees deja la culture du jeu video pour attirer de nouvelles recrues. En fevrier 2024, le journal The Guardian a rapporte que le Pentagone s'etait fixe pour objectif de rendre le service militaire plus attractif aupres des amateurs de jeux video , dans le but de faire appel a des gamers au sein de l'armee pour controler des armes a distance. Toujours selon le journal, differentes branches de l'armee ont constitue des equipes d'e-sportifs qui jouent a des jeux populaires aupres des enfants et des adolescents. Ce faisant, les militaires communiquent avec des mineurs dans le but de promouvoir le service militaire, en leur presentant la guerre comme un simple « jeu de tir ». Les militaires estiment que, si leurs efforts portent leurs fruits, les adolescents, une fois devenus adultes et ayant rejoint les rangs des forces armees, mettront finalement a profit les competences acquises grâce au jeu dans des conditions de combat, par exemple en tant qu'operateurs de drones. De tels cas se sont deja produits : en mai 2025, le New York Post a rapporte que des jeunes originaires des etats-Unis, du Royaume-Uni, du Canada, d'Australie et de France arrivaient en Ukraine pour rejoindre des unites utilisant des drones , alors que leur seule veritable qualification reside dans les annees passees devant leurs consoles de jeux.

items.title: JI warns it will expand ongoing sit-ins into wheel-jam, shutter-down strike
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Jamaat-i-Islami Pakistan (JI) Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman on Thursday warned that the JI would expand its ongoing sit-ins into a nationwide wheel-jam and shutter-down strike the week after 12th Rabiul Awwal (August 26) if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy. Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, he said the party would, in addition, establish protest camps across the country in support of its campaign. He said the JI could also march on Islamabad on foot if the government failed to respond to its demands. Rehman said he would address the sit-in in Lahore on Thursday, while a public gathering would be held at the Karachi protest venue on Friday. The JI chief said inflation had severely affected ordinary citizens, while the “Form 47 rulers” had failed to deliver basic services. He described the petroleum levy as an unjustified “extortionary tax”, saying consumers were paying around Rs80 per litre under the levy. According to him, the levy was originally introduced to finance the upgrading of Pakistan’s oil refineries. However, he said, the government had collected more than Rs8 trillion from consumers under the levy while spending less than Rs100 billion on refinery upgrades. Rehman said JI sit-ins in Lahore, Karachi and Peshawar were attracting increasing numbers of people, including traders, religious scholars, youth and civil society members. The protests, he said, had evolved into a platform for raising wider public grievances. “We want relief for the nation. The abolition of the levy is not a matter of our ego; it is a matter concerning the people,” he said, urging citizens to support the campaign. He urged Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to reduce petrol and diesel prices by Rs130, arguing that the government should pass the full benefit to consumers. The government had on Wednesday cut the price of high-speed diesel by Rs32.63 per litre and raised the price of petrol by Rs2.97 per litre. On a question about negotiations, Rehman said JI would not participate in government briefings and instead wanted the rulers to come to the protesters and engage directly with them. Recalling JI’s previous campaign against independent power producers (IPPs), Rehman said party workers had been stopped from entering Islamabad and subjected to tear-gas shelling before they established a sit-in in Rawalpindi. He said the government subsequently negotiated with JI and five IPPs were shut down and new agreements were signed with others, which he said saved the national exchequer Rs3.36 trillion. The party chief said 73 IPPs still needed to be reviewed and argued that meaningful negotiations with them could substantially reduce electricity prices within the next 12 to 18 months. He further said that IPPs were also being paid for electricity that was not generated, shifting the cost onto consumers. JI chief criticises rising taxes, cost of living The JI emir also criticised what he called the excessive privileges enjoyed by the ruling elite while low-income citizens faced rising taxes and living costs. He said the burden of the political elite’s expenditures was being borne by ordinary Pakistanis. Rehman said Pakistan’s total debt had risen to Rs98 trillion and called on the government to honour its commitments regarding the elimination of interest-based financing. He said reducing interest payments would help ease the country’s debt burden. He also criticised the power tariff structure, saying consumers continued to face excessive electricity bills while the government relied on additional charges to raise revenue. He questioned why the public should bear the cost when the Federal Board of Revenue’s 25,000 employees failed to meet their targets. Calling for austerity, he proposed that government vehicles should have engine capacities of no more than 1,300cc. He said corruption and unnecessary taxation must be eliminated. Turning to provincial governance, Rehman said the PPP had damaged Sindh and added that the PML-N had ruled Punjab for nearly four decades without resolving the province’s structural problems. He said poverty had significantly increased in Punjab. He also criticised Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s education policy, saying that 11,000 schools had been outsourced. “If you cannot run the education system, this is your failure,” he said. Addressing Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, he questioned the government’s priorities, saying it was unfair to impose the petroleum levy on ordinary citizens while allocating Rs11 billion for what he described as expenditure benefiting the prime minister’s niece. He also demanded the release of PTI founder Imran Khan and all political prisoners. He described restricting medical treatment for Imran as “fascism” and called for him to be provided with all necessary healthcare facilities. JI Vice-Emir Mian Muhammad Aslam, Deputy Secretary Syed Farasat Shah, Islamabad Emir Nasrullah Randhawa and Information Secretary Shakil Ahmed Turabi were also present at the press conference.

items.title: Sept morts dans le crash d’un hélicoptère touristique
items.description: Un hélicoptère de tourisme s’est écrasé, le mercredi 19 août 2026, près du mont Ololokwe, dans le comté de Samburu, au centre du Kenya. Les sept personnes à bord, dont un pilote kényan et six passagers, ont péri dans l’accident, selon l’Autorité kényane de l’aviation civile (KCAA). Le drame s’est produit lors d’un vol d’observation dans une zone montagneuse particulièrement prisée des randonneurs. L’appareil, un hélicoptère de type EC-130-B4, transportait sept personnes au moment de l’accident, dont son pilote, de nationalité kényane. Parmi les victimes figurent Michele Sensi-Contugi, présenté comme le chef du renseignement de l’Équateur et proche collaborateur du président Daniel Noboa, ainsi que son épouse, Stephany Hollihan. Les cinq autres passagers décédés étaient des ressortissants américains qui participaient à une excursion touristique. L’hélicoptère a été totalement détruit sous l’effet du choc et de l’incendie qui s’est déclaré après le crash. Les opérations de recherche et de récupération ont été rendues particulièrement difficiles par le relief accidenté de la zone et les conditions de visibilité. La Croix-Rouge kényane a notamment pris part aux opérations de secours. À la suite du crash, une enquête a été ouverte par l’Autorité kényane d’investigation sur les accidents aériens (AAID). Les investigations doivent permettre d’établir les circonstances et les causes exactes de ce crash qui endeuille le secteur touristique au Kenya. Alors que les autorités kényanes poursuivent les recherches d’éléments susceptibles d’éclairer le drame, l’enquête de l’AAID devra désormais déterminer ce qui a conduit l’hélicoptère à s’écraser dans cette région montagneuse de Samburu. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Sept morts dans le crash d’un hélicoptère touristique est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Why prescribe drugs by brand name? Pharmacists call for change after child endangered by drug dispensing error
items.description: Last week, seven-year-old Mecca came down with a cold and a sore throat. She visited her doctor for examination, and was prescribed a nutritional supplement to help with the symptoms. Her family sent a photo of the prescription to a pharmacy in Zahraa al-Maadi for home delivery, and the drug was delivered around 11:30 pm. After ingesting a 6-ml dose of the drug, however, Mecca “suffered something akin to paralysis,” her mother, Samia, tells Mada Masr. “My daughter was suffering from a simple cold,” says Samia. “But the pharmacist confused the last two letters [of the drug’s name] and dispensed an epilepsy medication instead.” Samia rushed her daughter to the Poison Control Center, which refused to admit Mecca, as did several hospitals afterward, with all of them telling the mother that, since it had been 24 hours since the medication was administered, she needed to go to the intensive care unit at Demerdash Hospital, where the specialized care unit is located. Mecca remained sick for a day and a half, “no longer able to move her hands, legs or eyes,” Samia says. She remained in this condition for four days before eventually recovering. Soon after the life-threatening incident, the family filed a lawsuit against the pharmacy and submitted complaints to the Egyptian Drug Authority — the body responsible for pharmacy inspections — as well as to the Pharmacists Syndicate and the public prosecutor. But professionals working in the pharmacy sector and syndicate officials who spoke to Mada Masr say Mecca’s case is not the first time a patient has faced dangerous consequences as a result of mistakes in interpreting prescriptions. For them, complaints and investigations into each individual incident — while important for establishing liability and holding the responsible party accountable — will fail to address the root cause of the problem or prevent its recurrence, leaving patients exposed to the same danger. They believe the true solution lies in changing prescribing practices: mandating that physicians prescribe medications by their generic, non-proprietary names to reduce the likelihood that pharmacists will confuse the commercial names of popular drugs, a demand that pharmacists have put to the Health Ministry in recent days and which has already been recommended in a 2024 prime ministerial directive. However, doctors have expressed unwillingness to adhere to the recommendation — a stance that several sources who spoke to Mada Masr attribute to the strong financial and professional incentives offered by pharmaceutical companies to doctors, part of marketing arrangements that generate billions in revenue. *** Mistakes in drug dispensation of the kind that endangered Samia’s daughter are easily made when doctors prescribe drugs by their commercial name, according to two pharmacists who spoke to Mada Masr. A Pharmacists Syndicate official, speaking on condition of anonymity, tells Mada Masr that Mecca would not have been endangered had the generic name been used. The confusion originated due to a confusion between the name of the prescribed drug and a different drug with a similar name, he says. “The active ingredient in the first medication, Acetylcysteine, is completely different from the one in the second medication, Risperidone, which is used to treat certain psychiatric and neurological disorders,” he explains. A pharmacy manager notes that by contrast the trade name for the prescribed drug, Respidep, is very similar to Risperdal, the brand name of the antipsychotic that was dispensed. “Similar incidents have occurred many times,” says the pharmacy manager. “One case that stands out in my memory involved a pharmacist who mistakenly dispensed a neurological medication: the difference between the name written on the prescription and the drug actually dispensed was just two letters.” A bare minimum threshold to prevent the recurrence of similar incidents would be to mandate that doctors use generic names, says the manager, who stresses that “there is no active ingredient whose name resembles another active ingredient in the way brand names do.” Brand names, by contrast, are frequently very similar, he says, noting that companies will often exploit the name recognition of existing medication, launching drugs under similar brand names that differ by a couple of letters. There are myriad examples of similar trade names, such as antispasmodic drugs Spasomofin and Spasmomen, or deworming medication Flubvendazole and Metronidazole, an antibiotic. Given that doctors often have illegible handwriting, the similarity of trade names increases the chance of misreading, whether on the part of the physician or the pharmacist. Opting for the name of the active ingredient could reduce the margin for error when reading prescriptions and dispensing medication, says the pharmacy manager. A simple solution would be for the doctor to write the scientific name of the active ingredient alongside the brand name of the specific drug they want, he says. But he anticipates that the widespread adoption of this practice is unlikely. “A doctor might feel embarrassed to do that, as it would make them look like a dealer doing business with [pharma] companies,” he says. With many physicians prescribing drugs by their commercial name rather than their active ingredients, doctors play a major role in the pharmaceutical market and sales. Companies strive to persuade doctors to prescribe their pharmaceutical products over market alternatives, relying on a nationwide network of sales representatives and massive advertising budgets which aim to convince the largest possible number of doctors to prescribe these drugs. This “persuasion” goes beyond scientific arguments claiming one product is superior to its alternative, relying instead on a range of incentives that companies offer to doctors. These range from facilitating participation in scientific conferences — in Egypt and abroad — to, in some instances, direct cash payments in exchange for prescribing specific products, thereby encouraging the doctor’s continued commitment to the practice despite the potential negative impact on patients. *** While the Cairo Pharmacists Syndicate has already requested government action to enforce an existing ministerial directive that says doctors should use generic names, the response from physicians has been lukewarm. After Mecca’s hospitalization, the syndicate said last week that it had sent a formal request to the health minister calling for a mandate that all medical service providers prescribe drugs using generic rather than brand names in accordance with the prime minister’s 2024 directives. They proposed it be implemented as an immediate, specific and binding measure for antibiotics as a first step, to help curb their indiscriminate and excessive use, limit the dangers of antibiotic resistance, and accurately assess and monitor treatment efficacy. This measure would grant patients the freedom to choose between commercial alternatives of the same generic drug, breaking the monopoly that expensive brand names hold and ensuring the availability of alternatives during drug shortages. It would also help patients obtain substitutes quickly, without much back-and-forth between physicians and pharmacies, the syndicate said. The step would “represent a qualitative shift in national pharmaceutical policy,” the syndicate said, “and strengthen state sovereignty in providing safe, effective medicines at fair prices,” requesting that the health minister order a review of the proposal and issue an urgent directive for its adoption. In a separate request to the health minister, the syndicate asked that public and private healthcare facilities be required to issue prescriptions digitally to reduce errors resulting from illegible handwriting or similarities in drug names and dosages. But when Mada Masr asked officials from the Doctors Syndicate whether they would welcome the step, they were unenthusiastic. Doctors are “committed to the patient’s best interest” and to ensuring they receive effective treatment, says Khaled Amin, assistant secretary general and board member at the union. Consequently, they will prescribe the medication they deem most suitable for the patient’s condition, including specific brand names, he says, maintaining that the “patient’s best interest” is not necessarily served by relying solely on generic drugs. Denying that the practice of prescribing specific brands is linked to financial incentives by the pharmaceutical industry, he argues that “no one would jeopardize their reputation just because a company is offering a trip.” On using generic names, he believes it is impossible for a doctor to be certain of the details. “I am a doctor,” he says, “and I cannot memorize all the generic names: there are so many of them.” Gamal Omera, a member of the Doctors Syndicate board, also tells Mada Masr that he believes it would be difficult in practice to mandate that prescriptions are written using generic names. Brand names are often short and easy to use, he says, whereas generic names can consist of multiple syllables, making them long and difficult to write, citing the GSK-made Augmentin as an example, noting that the drug’s generic name is far longer than the well-known brand. Both Doctors Syndicate officials believe a digital prescription system is a long way off, with Amin describing it as “impossible at present.” It would require digital infrastructure connecting all service providers and digital records for every patient, he explains, along with many preparatory steps. Doctors can use printed prescriptions if they wish, he says, though they cannot currently be required to, particularly in medical convoys and rural areas where computers and printers may be less available. *** Mahmoud Fouad, chair of patient advocacy organization Right to Medicine, believes that prescribing by generic name would indeed “reduce the confusion that currently occurs.” But he anticipates that the shared interests of doctors and pharmaceutical companies will prevent such a practice from being widely adopted. Demanding generic drug prescriptions is “like stirring up a hornet’s nest,” he says. “Companies would raise an outcry, and the state would be unable to confront them due to commercial competition, investments and the influence of major corporations — particularly those that do business with doctors.” Ultimately, he concludes, “it is a losing battle for pharmacists.” All the health and pharmacy professionals and experts who spoke to Mada Masr agree that improvements at the pharmacy level are possible. Mahfouz Ramzy, head of the Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Committee of the Pharmacists Syndicate, assures Mada Masr that the complaint filed by Mecca’s father to the syndicate last week has been referred to the Legal Affairs Department, and that an investigative committee, including a representative from the State Council, has been assigned to the case. While it remains unclear whether the pharmacy that dispensed the medication to Mecca’s family made an error beyond misreading the drug’s name, there are various loopholes that could be closed, the sources suggest. Fouad and Amin, for example, both note that many pharmacies operate without a qualified pharmacist present, meaning that even if the prescription uses a generic name, a pharmacy assistant might still be unable to read and dispense the right drug. However, the pharmacy manager suggests that the margin for improvement here is limited as the law mandates a pharmacist be present but does not require that they themselves take exclusive responsibility for dispensing medications. This is consistent with how the Egyptian Drug Authority itself conducts inspections, he explains, with the primary concern often being simply to verify the presence of a licensed pharmacist. Some pharmacy job advertisements explicitly seek a “morning pharmacist for inspection times,” he continues, implying that, in some cases, the pharmacist’s presence is tied more to regulatory compliance than practicing the profession. He says that while any pharmacist can make a dispensing error, “it is certainly a grave mistake.” A more effective corrective measure, he proposes, would be stricter experience requirements for pharmacists responsible for dispensing medication. The presence of a pharmacist with extensive experience —”eight years, for instance”— could help reduce errors in reading prescriptions and distinguishing between look-alike medications. But he stresses that holding pharmacies alone responsible for the error will not prevent similar mistakes from happening again — a view shared by the syndicate official. “The primary objective of mandating generic prescription must be patient protection,” the pharmacy owner concludes, pointing to the Health Ministry as the entity primarily responsible for enforcing this measure. The post Why prescribe drugs by brand name? Pharmacists call for change after child endangered by drug dispensing error first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: Session de rattrapage du bac 2026 : plus de 20 mille candidats rescapés dans les starting-blocks
items.description: Une nouvelle page s’ouvre dans l’histoire du système éducatif guinéen. Ce jeudi 20 août 2026, le lycée de Coléah, dans la commune de Matam, a servi de cadre au lancement des épreuves de la première session de rattrapage du baccalauréat. Une initiative inédite destinée à offrir une seconde chance aux candidats qui n’ont pas réussi à décrocher le précieux diplôme lors de la session ordinaire. Pour cette première expérience, les autorités éducatives entendent permettre aux candidats ayant échoué de peu de retenter leur chance. À travers cette session exceptionnelle, le Gouvernement souhaite ainsi offrir une nouvelle opportunité à ceux qui étaient proches de la moyenne requise pour décrocher le baccalauréat au titre de la session 2026. Présent au lycée de Coléah pour le lancement des épreuves, Dr Julien Bongono, Secrétaire général du ministère de l’Éducation nationale, de l’Alphabétisation, de l’Enseignement technique et de la Formation professionnelle, a expliqué le bien-fondé de cette nouvelle mesure. Selon lui, les candidats concernés ne sont pas nécessairement en difficulté sur le plan académique, mais n’ont simplement pas réussi à franchir le cap lors de la première session. « C’est une première dans notre système. Cette initiative a été prise par le Gouvernement pour permettre aux candidats qui sont passés très près, qui n’ont pas eu la moyenne, d’avoir une chance de pouvoir obtenir le baccalauréat de cette session », a-t-il expliqué. Face aux candidats réunis dans les salles d’examen, le message des autorités a surtout été celui de la confiance et de la détermination. Au nom de la ministre en charge de l’Éducation nationale, le secrétaire général les a invités à saisir pleinement cette opportunité et à croire davantage en leurs capacités. « S’ils sont là, effectivement, c’est parce qu’ils ont le niveau », a-t-il rappelé, appelant les candidats à aborder les épreuves avec sérénité et confiance. Au-delà du caractère inédit de cette session, une précision majeure a été apportée concernant la valeur du diplôme délivré aux candidats admis. Le baccalauréat obtenu à l’issue de la session de rattrapage aura exactement la même valeur que celui obtenu lors de la session ordinaire. Cette garantie revêt une importance particulière pour les candidats, puisqu’elle leur permettra de bénéficier des mêmes conditions d’admission dans les établissements d’enseignement supérieur. Il ne s’agit donc pas d’un diplôme au rabais, mais bien du même baccalauréat, avec les mêmes droits et les mêmes perspectives académiques. « Les diplômes qu’ils vont obtenir ont la même valeur que le baccalauréat de la session ordinaire. C’est quelque chose d’important puisque cela permet d’accéder effectivement aux mêmes conditions d’admission dans l’enseignement supérieur », a souligné Dr Julien Bongono. Pour les autorités éducatives, l’enjeu est également de garantir la crédibilité de cette première session de rattrapage. C’est dans cette optique qu’une délégation composée notamment de membres du cabinet du ministère s’est rendue au lycée de Coléah afin de constater de visu les dispositifs mis en place pour la passation des épreuves. L’exigence affichée est claire : les conditions d’organisation et de surveillance doivent répondre aux mêmes standards que ceux appliqués lors de la session ordinaire. Il en va de la crédibilité du processus, mais également de la valeur du diplôme qui sera attribué aux futurs admis. À l’issue de la visite, les autorités se sont dites rassurées par les dispositions prises. Selon elles, les services compétents ont mis en place les mesures nécessaires pour assurer un déroulement régulier des épreuves sur l’ensemble des sites concernés. Cette session de rattrapage constitue ainsi une nouvelle voie offerte aux candidats qui n’ont pas pu concrétiser leurs efforts lors de la première session. Pour eux, les épreuves qui ont débuté ce jeudi représentent bien plus qu’un simple examen : elles constituent une véritable seconde chance et, pour certains, la possibilité de tourner définitivement la page du secondaire avec le précieux sésame en poche. Faut-il enfin rappeler que cette session de rattrapage du bac 2026 dont les épreuves ont été lancées ce jeudi s’achèvera le 23 août. Ils sont au total 20763 candidats dont 9 336 filles à tenter une dernière fois leur chance.

items.title: The New History Wars
items.description: On a recent afternoon in Washington, I put on a pair of augmented-reality glasses for a tour of some very recent ruins: the White House East Wing. In recent months, black fencing has overtaken the area, where Donald Trump’s ballroom construction is speeding along as the Supreme Court decides its fate. Visitors can’t see much of anything from the street. As I wore the clunky eyewear, though, historic images of the structure flashed in front of me. The glasses showed me features wiped away by the president during his ongoing renovation spree, such as the Jacqueline Kennedy Garden and the White House Family Theater. Looking around, I could see a panorama of images visualizing Trump’s plans to transform Washington, D.C.: the Reflecting Pool, the Triumphal Arch, the Eisenhower Executive Office Building, and more. The tour guide, a public historian named Lexi Cleveland, created this very 2026 experience as the executive vice president of ARtGlass, an AR company. (One of the co-founders is Greg Werkheiser, a cultural-heritage lawyer currently suing the Trump administration over plans to paint the Eisenhower Executive Office Building.) Cleveland prompted me with questions throughout. “What do we actually lose when we lose a building?” she asked. When the glasses showed me a Black Lives Matter mural that the city removed after Trump’s return to office, Cleveland juxtaposed it with the equestrian statue of President Andrew Jackson in front of the White House. The populist Jackson is one of Trump’s favorite presidents; expanding slavery and signing the Indian Removal Act are inextricable parts of his legacy. The construction of the statue, completed in 1852, involved an enslaved apprentice. “If you got to decide,” Cleveland asked, “does the statue stay, go, get contextualized with signage, or get moved to a museum?” She plans to ask these questions to larger groups when the tours start in full this month, and she’s prepared to mediate debates. The approach feels fitting in a country engaged in an active struggle over how to remember its past. History is on Trump’s mind. He wants to become part of it by reshaping the commemorative landscape of Washington. And he wants to reframe how history is told within Washington’s museums. For over a year, the White House has scolded and threatened the Smithsonian. But last month, the president took an unprecedented step toward pushing that feud into the real world. In an executive order , he called on the National Park Service to place signs outside the National Museum of American History, which the White House has said is subject to “ideological capture” at the hands of “a radical activist cohort.” The Park Service will direct visitors to “accurate information” about the nation’s past and mount its own temporary exhibit about the signatories of the Declaration of Independence, who the White House says aren’t showcased enough by the museum. The fight for public memory will soon spill into the streets. [ Read: The capital is a mess ] It will happen on the National Mall, where the National Guard continues to roam and not far from the transformed White House, with its abundant fencing—at this point, a core aesthetic of the second Trump administration. Across town, scaffolding outside the Kennedy Center blocks the part of the facade where Trump’s name once hung above the late president’s. Historic statues at Arlington Memorial Bridge have been swallowed up by blindin g gold . Meanwhile, at two plazas in downtown Washington, statues that came down during the Black Lives Matter protests have been reinstalled: One of Confederate General Albert Pike returned to Judiciary Square last fall, and one of Caesar Rodney (which was toppled in Wilmington, Delaware), who signed the Declaration of Independence and enslaved hundreds of people, now overlooks Freedom Plaza. Historians, preservationists, and activists are finding ways to work their own ideas and stories back into public space, in spite of the obstacles. The most visible example might be a series of viral art pieces by the guerilla art group the Secret Handshake that keep appearing on the Mall. (In March, the group plopped a gold toilet by the Lincoln Memorial to poke fun at Trump’s redevelopment projects.) But there are more sober ventures too. When Trump’s exhibit goes up outside the American History Museum, a group called Citizen Historians for the Smithsonian plans to send docents to “interpret” the signage for visitors—a nerdy form of counter-protest. Even the Smithsonian American Women’s History Museum, which has not yet been assigned a site because of partisan fighting in Congress, is oddly of a piece with this renegade spirit: It has resorted to an augmented-reality exhibit that dreams up some new monuments for D.C. The projects get at the central disagreement fueling these feuds over history: whether, as Trump sees it, American history is best told through a simple, sweeping narrative of grandeur or, as these groups see it, through a compendium of diverse stories. If the city suddenly feels like it’s in rough-draft form, Trump isn’t the only one with a red pen in hand. A few days after Trump issued his executive order about the National Museum of American History, I arrived at a very wholesome protest: about a dozen concerned museumgoers holding signs outside the staff entrance to the building and singing patriotic songs such as “My Country, ’Tis of Thee.” The makeshift choir is part of a larger group, Citizen Historians for the Smithsonian, that came together last year to archive material across the Smithsonian because it feared that the Trump administration might start altering exhibits. I found one of Citizen Historians’ leaders, Jessica Dickinson Goodman, explaining the recent drama to a group of tourists, a kind of test run for conversations to come. Earlier this month, the group’s role expanded from DIY archivists to rogue docents when it put out a call for help interpreting the signage that Trump is adding to the Mall. In its newsletter, the group described the effort as nonconfrontational and fact-based. Dozens of volunteers came forward. Dickinson Goodman told me that they’re creating instructions for the types of topics that might arise: “We’ll start showing up as soon as we hear of construction starting.” [ Read: Trump’s trigger warnings ] One place where the grand, old-school version of history that the Trump administration seems to prefer prevails in the monuments and memorials on the National Mall. Here, the subject matter is clear, and the tone, though solemn, is usually celebratory. The sole memorial dedicated to a named historical woman is for Eleanor Roosevelt, though the statue is incorporated into her husband’s larger commemorative site. For its 250th celebration, the Smithsonian American Women’s History Museum put out its augmented-reality exhibit, “Unhidden Heroines,” to highlight five women associated with five major monuments—and to underscore their absence from public art. It’s hard not to perceive an exhibition squished onto your phone screen as an indicator of where women’s history stands these days. Still, it’s worth a “visit.” At the Jefferson Memorial, the geotagged exhibition focuses on Mary Katharine Goddard, who printed the first copy of the Declaration of Independence to list most of the signers. At the Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial, Dorothy Height talks about how she helped organize the March on Washington but did not speak at it. At the end of each anecdote, a “monument” of sorts pops up next to whatever your camera is pointing at. The figures appear so large on the screen, they sometimes dwarf the actual monuments. “That was intentional, of course, because they were towering women in their own right,” Karri Nussle, the museum’s associate director for advancement and external affairs, told me. It was fun. Well done too. But sitting there with my phone and my headphones and the make-believe monuments, I also felt kind of sad. Eventually, the augmented-reality glasses come off. The phone screen goes black. The volunteer docents go home. What’s left? At the Jefferson Memorial, after I put my phone down, sending a cartoonish Mary Katharine Goddard back into the digital ether, it was just me and the man cast in bronze.

items.title: WHO, Africa CDC welcome allocation of Ebola vaccines to DRC
items.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) and the Africa Centers for Disease and Prevention Control (Africa CDC) have welcomed the allocation of tens of thousands of doses of Merck's Ervebo Ebola vaccine to the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The International Coordinating Group on Vaccine Provision (ICG) on Monday informed the DRC government of an immediate initial release of 70,000 doses, including 20,000 doses for a Phase 3 clinical trial to understand the impact of the vaccine on the Bundibugyo virus, and 50,000 doses for frontline and health workers. Ervebo is licensed and recommended for preventing Ebola disease caused by the Zaire ebolavirus. However, there is currently no approved vaccine or treatment specifically for the Bundibugyo virus. The WHO said it is not yet known whether Ervebo can protect humans against Bundibugyo, although early laboratory and animal studies suggest it may offer some protection. The clinical trial is expected to provide evidence that could guide future use of the vaccine against the virus. "Africa CDC and WHO are united in support of the Government of the DRC, to protect affected communities, save lives and bring the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak to an end, while generating the scientific evidence needed to strengthen Africa's preparedness for future outbreaks," said a statement by the two agencies released on Thursday. Health authorities have reiterated that people receiving the vaccine must be informed about its potential risks, benefits and limitations and provide informed consent, particularly those participating in the clinical trial. Government data shows that confirmed Ebola cases in the DRC have now surpassed 5,000, with the death toll reaching 2,378. The outbreak became the country's largest on record in late July, overtaking the previous worst epidemic recorded between 2018 and 2020. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said earlier this week that the outbreak remains a global emergency.

items.title: Guéckédou : Isaac Lelano élu maire à l’unanimité
items.description: La commune urbaine de Guéckédou vient de connaître son nouveau maire. Conformément aux dispositions du Code électoral, l’élection s’est tenue ce jeudi 20 août 2026 et a consacré la victoire de Isaac Lelano à la tête de la municipalité, succédant au défunt maire Anathin Siafa Kamano. ​Seul candidat en lice, Isaac Lelano a recueilli l’adhésion unanime du conseil communal. Selon les témoignages recueillis auprès des conseillers électeurs, le scrutin s’est déroulé dans un climat de paix, de sérénité et de responsabilité, se soldant par 35 voix favorables et un unique bulletin nul. ​Placée sous la présidence et la vigilance du préfet, le général Kandja Mara, ainsi qu’en présence de responsables militaires, la séance s’est distinguée par la rigueur de son encadrement et le civisme de l’ensemble des participants. ​Au-delà de la victoire électorale, cette journée a été saluée pour l’esprit de sagesse et de solidarité qui l’a animée. Pour plusieurs observateurs locaux, le large consensus dégagé autour de la candidature d'Isaac Lelano témoigne d'une volonté partagée de privilégier l’intérêt général de la commune et de consolider la cohésion sociale. ​Cette élection met fin à une période de transition et d’attente. Pour la cité de Guéckédou, un nouveau chapitre s’ouvre désormais, assorti d’importants défis à relever : la modernisation des infrastructures, l’accès aux services sociaux de base, l’assainissement urbain et l’amélioration du cadre de vie des populations. ​Désormais remobilisée autour de sa nouvelle équipe dirigeante, Guéckédou ambitionne de transformer le climat d'apaisement qui a prévalu durant ce scrutin en une dynamique durable de développement au service de tous ses citoyens.

items.title: Importations : les Douanes algériennes lancent le guichet électronique unique, ce qui change
items.description: Une nouvelle démarche est entreprise par la douane algérienne dans le sens de la dématérialisation des procédures relatives au commerce extérieur. Désormais, les autorisations administratives délivrées par le ministère du Commerce extérieur doivent être introduites via un “guichet électronique unique”, comme le dévoile un avis de l’inspection divisionnaire des douanes d’Alger (commerce), destiné aux commissionnaires en douane et paru le 18 août dernier. Mis en service du “guichet électronique unique” L’inspection indique que le “guichet électronique unique” du système d’information des douanes (ALCES) qui permet de faire ses formalités douanières en ligne a été “mis en service”, notant qu’il s’agit d’un module dédié “aux autorisations et certificats administratifs exigés lors du dédouanement”. Mais qu’est-ce que cela change concrètement ? Les commissionnaires en douane doivent désormais “introduire les autorisations administratives du ministère du Commerce via le guichet unique”, en plus de se soumettre à la procédure habituelle (support papier). Le document souligne en effet que cette dématérialisation de la procédure se fera “parallèlement au processus manuel, et ce, en attendant la suppression totale du support papier”. Qu’est-ce que cela signifie ? Boubaker Seddik Arrar, responsable administratif en finances et comptabilité explique qu’il s’agit d’une “mise en service progressive” du module “guichet unique électronique”, assurant que cette démarche vise “la suppression totale du support papier dans un avenir proche”. Selon lui, ce changement tend à “simplifier, accélérer et sécuriser les opérations de dédouanement en centralisant toutes les autorisations dans un système unique et digital”, a-t-il écrit dans un post LinkedIn. Contacté par TSA, un autre expert précise que “cet avis concerne l'introduction des formalités administratives particulières habituelles qui touchent certains produits selon leur nature”. Il confirme ensuite que cette démarche, qui vise à introduire ces formalités sur le système informatique de la douane via la mise en place d’un guichet électronique unique, vise à “accélérer la délivrance des diverses autorisations et visas, lutter contre la corruption, les transferts illicites de capitaux et le trafic de documents, contrôler les documents transmis sur ALCES, réduire la paperasse ainsi qu’à mieux maîtriser et contrôler les valeurs”. Pour finir, cet expert dévoile que plusieurs institutions seront concernées par ce changement, notamment “les directions de commerces, les services phytosanitaires au poste frontière, les services vétérinaires, ONML, ONDA, ministère des hydrocarbures …”. Le guichet unique électronique modifie la donne dans les relations entre les Douanes et les opérateurs économiques. « Avant le guichet électronique unique, il fallait s'adresser à l’organisme concerné, accompagné des originaux des documents nécessaires, et ce à l’arrivée de la marchandise au port. L’établissement de l’autorisation peut prendre 20 jours et parfois beaucoup plus. Maintenant avec le guichet unique et ALCES, le temps est compté, ce qui représente une avancée importante », explique-t-il. L’article Importations : les Douanes algériennes lancent le guichet électronique unique, ce qui change est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: JUI-F chief, opposition leaders agree to form ‘united opposition’
items.description: An agreement was reached in principle on Thursday between Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas to form a “united opposition”, a spokesperson for the opposition alliance Tehreek Tahafuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP) said in a statement. The JUI-F chief met the opposition leaders in the National Assembly and Senate in the opposition chamber at Parliament House in Islamabad, where they discussed the country’s current political situation, parliamentary affairs, cooperation among opposition parties and future political strategy, the spokesperson said. The participants in the meetings expressed concern over and condemned the “government’s attitude and behaviour towards the opposition in the National Assembly and Senate,” he added. “The opposition leaders said that in a democracy, the opposition’s voice is heard, not suppressed.” According to the opposition alliance, the meeting also considered the “policies being adopted by the government, the role of the opposition in parliament, and the future strategy for protecting the Constitution and democracy”. “Fazl and Achakzai also exchanged views on making contacts among opposition parties more effective and adopting a joint strategy at the parliamentary level,” the statement said. Moreover, it was agreed to continue “further consultations among opposition parties and formulate a joint course of action”, it elaborated. “During the meeting, serious concern was expressed over the health of PTI founder Imran Khan,” the spokesperson said, adding, “The opposition leaders demanded that, in light of the Supreme Court decision , Imran Khan be transferred to a hospital at the earliest and provided with the best possible medical treatment.” “The opposition leaders said that no politics should be played on the issue of the former prime minister’s health; he should be provided with immediate and appropriate medical facilities on humanitarian and medical grounds.” PTI leader and former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser also participated in the meeting. The JUI-F delegation included MNA Uthman Badini, Senator Kamran Murad, Senator Maulana Abdul Wasay and Maulana Kamaluddin. PTI parliamentary leader Shahid Khattak, Chief Whip Malik Amir Dogar, MNAs Atif Khan, Shehram Khan Tarakai, Sanaullah Masti Khel and Ali Asghar Khan, and MPA Asif Khan Mehsud were also present at the meeting. Meanwhile, speaking to the media after the meeting, the JUI-F chief said that today’s meeting was the first between the opposition parties and that they had decided that a “united opposition would be formed”. “This was the first session, and further consultations will also take place. All opposition parties will come together to form the opposition,” Fazl said. He added that contacts among the opposition parties would be strengthened and a joint strategy would be finalised. “The matter of holding an All Parties Conference should also be discussed,” he said. On Wednesday, the PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, also had a meeting with the opposition leaders, along with a PPP delegation. The meeting discussed parliamentary affairs and the country’s political situation. Bilawal asked the opposition leaders to join parliamentary committees and play an active role, according to the statement. The participants also agreed to maintain contact and cooperate on legislative matters in the parliament.

items.title: Transformation digitale : Faya Bourouno défend la modernisation de l’administration guinéenne
items.description: La transformation numérique de l’administration guinéenne s’accélère. Lors d’une conférence de presse tenue ce mercredi, le ministre de la Modernisation de l’Administration et de la Fonction publique, également porte-parole du gouvernement, Faya François Bourouno, a présenté plusieurs plateformes numériques mises en place pour améliorer l’efficacité, la traçabilité et l’accessibilité des services publics. Selon le ministre, ces différents outils traduisent la volonté des autorités de construire « un État moderne » et s’inscrivent dans la dynamique de la refondation de l’État portée par le président de la République. Dans le secteur minier, Faya Bourouno a notamment cité Damanda, une plateforme destinée à dématérialiser la gestion du cadastre et des titres miniers. Elle permet, selon lui, de rendre les demandes et les décisions « traçables, vérifiables en temps réel » et de réduire les délais de délivrance des actes. Une évolution qui doit contribuer, d’après le ministre, à renforcer l’attractivité du climat des affaires et la transparence dans la gestion des ressources minières. Autre chantier présenté : Telemou, consacré à la commande publique. La plateforme couvre désormais l’ensemble du cycle de passation des marchés, depuis l’appel d’offres jusqu’à l’évaluation, l’attribution et le suivi de l’exécution. Pour Faya Bourouno, cette digitalisation revêt un enjeu majeur, alors que les marchés publics représenteraient entre 11 et 15 % de la richesse nationale. Dans le domaine des finances publiques, le ministre a évoqué SONEYA, qui vise à fluidifier et sécuriser les procédures d’exécution du budget de l’État. Cette plateforme est complétée par TrésorPay, qui permet notamment aux citoyens ne disposant pas de compte bancaire d’effectuer des paiements liés à certains services administratifs. A en croire Faya François Bourouno, la gestion des effectifs et de la masse salariale constitue également un autre volet de cette transformation numérique. Le gouvernement, selon son porte-parole, s’appuie désormais sur le Fichier Unique de Gestion Administrative et de la Solde (FUGAS), présenté comme un outil permettant de fiabiliser les données relatives aux agents publics et à la masse salariale. Mais c’est surtout GEDAF, dédiée à la gestion électronique des actes administratifs et normatifs, que le porte-parole du gouvernement a particulièrement mise en avant. Une plateforme qui dématérialiserait la chaîne de conception et de traitement des décisions, arrêtés et décrets. Réagissant aux commentaires selon lesquels la décision du chef de l’État de suivre directement GEDAF depuis son bureau traduirait une volonté de « reprendre la main », Faya Bourouno a défendu une autre lecture. Pour lui, il ne s’agit nullement d’un revirement, puisque ces outils ont été institués sur instruction du président de la République. « On ne reprend pas la main sur ce que l’on a soi-même institué », a-t-il déclaré, estimant que l’implication du chef de l’État s’inscrit plutôt dans une logique de suivi et de pilotage des réformes. En outre, le ministre a établi un lien direct entre ces plateformes numériques, le programme Simandou 2040 et la vision présidentielle de développement. Il a expliqué que le processus repose sur plusieurs étapes : l’élaboration du programme, sa transmission aux membres du gouvernement comme feuille de route, le lancement des projets, puis l’accélération des processus normatifs afin d’éviter les retards et les blocages administratifs. Pour Faya Bourouno, la digitalisation de l’administration ne constitue donc pas une série d’initiatives isolées, mais une composante d’une stratégie globale visant à rendre l’État guinéen plus efficace, transparent et capable d’assurer un meilleur suivi de ses décisions et de ses ressources.

items.description: La region de Segou dispose desormais de son vestibule des autorites et legitimites traditionnelles. items.title: Trump's 'economic war' on Iran faces question marks over impact
items.description: US President Donald Trump on Wednesday announced what he called the "most crushing economic operation ever" against Iran, one he said would amount to "economic warfare." Experts said the move reflects Washington's attempt to shift from military pressure to economic coercion amid a deadlock in US-Iran tensions, while its actual impact remains uncertain. They questioned whether the sanctions can be effectively implemented and achieve their intended goals, noting that decades of US sanctions against Iran have failed to force Tehran's hand. Trump said in a social media post that any country allowing its financial institutions, businesses, airports or government structures to support Tehran will face massive economic consequences. He called for an immediate halt to activities including "oil smuggling," currency exchanges, cash transfers, vessel registrations and the use of shell companies while urging US allies to join Washington in isolating Tehran. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent last week warned that Washington would soon unveil "unprecedented" measures to economically isolate Iran alongside efforts to block the Strait of Hormuz and prevent goods from entering or leaving Iranian ports. From military pressure to economic coercion Li Zixin, an assistant research fellow at the China Institute of International Studies, said Washington's turn toward economic warfare stems largely from the limited effectiveness of military action and the difficulty of achieving further breakthroughs in the short term. Since the conflict began in late February, the US military has rapidly consumed various types of missiles, with defensive ammunition stockpiles under particular pressure, Li said. At the same time, US assets in the Middle East and the security of American allies have faced mounting challenges. Domestic political pressure has also pushed the Trump administration to adjust its approach, Li said. Since the conflict began, at least 18 US service members have been killed, nearly $40 billion has been spent, and US gasoline prices have risen by nearly 40% from pre-conflict levels. With the midterm elections approaching, the growing costs of the conflict have become a political burden for the White House. "This is a strategic shift after military measures failed to achieve political objectives, rather than the administration's preferred option from the outset," Li said. He also cast doubt on the potential impact of the sanctions, saying higher oil prices could create new pressure on global markets and American consumers. Meanwhile, Iran's decades of experience dealing with sanctions has enabled it to develop resilient mechanisms to circumvent restrictions, further limiting the effectiveness of economic pressure, he said. Implementation remains uncertain Qin Tian, deputy director of the Institute of Middle East Studies at the China Institutes of Contemporary International Relations, said the economic measures outlined by Trump largely represent a "repetition of old tactics." "Currently, we have not seen the US government, particularly the Treasury Department, release specific details. Sanctions require concrete implementation procedures and mechanisms," Qin said. He noted that many of Trump's announced measures on Wednesday are similar to policies Washington has already pursued in recent years. "Due to the long-standing US sanctions regime, foreign governments, institutions and financial organizations have already significantly reduced direct economic ties with Iran. The room for requiring other countries to cooperate with US sanctions is actually quite limited," Qin said. He also pointed to previous examples of gaps between Washington's policy announcements and actual implementation. Shortly after returning to the White House, Trump signed a memorandum aimed at reducing Iran's oil exports to "zero," but that goal was not achieved in the following years. In February, the Trump administration also issued an executive order calling for a 25% "secondary tariff" on countries importing Iranian goods, including services, but the measure was never fully implemented. "Although the newly announced measures appear aggressive, their actual implementation remains uncertain," Qin said. He added that the US military campaign failed to force Iran into submission, while diplomatic efforts also failed to secure concessions from Tehran. "Under these circumstances, Trump has returned to economic sanctions to demonstrate its tough stance," Qin said. "He may hope that economic pressure will eventually force Iran to make concessions, but the outcome remains highly uncertain."

items.title: Transferts : Salifou Soumah prêté au Panetolikos FC par Malmö
items.description: Salifou Soumah enchaîne les prêts. Après le Radomiak Radom (Pologne), l’attaquant guinéen vient de filer en prêt au Panetolikos FC, pensionnaire de la première division grecque. Ce prêt de l'ancien joueur de l’AS Kaloum court jusqu'en juin 2027, assorti d'une option d’achat. Philip Berglund, le directeur sportif du club suédois souligne que : « Salifou a besoin de temps de jeu et, compte tenu de la concurrence et de notre changement de cap stratégique, il sera difficile de s’imposer à Malmö. Cet accord est bénéfique pour toutes les parties et nous souhaitons à Salifou bonne chance en Grèce ! ». Salifou Soumah s’est révélé à l’AS Kaloum avant de rejoindre le Havre, en France. Il a rejoint Malmö en juin 2025, en provenance du Zira FK, de l’Azerbaïdjan. L’attaquant guinéen a disputé 12 matchs officiels avec le club suédois. items.title: Peut-on faire confiance aux captures d’écran ?
items.description: Listen to « Peut-on faire confiance aux captures d'ecran ? (education numerique) » on Spreaker. Une capture d'ecran peut sembler parfaitement authentique sans pour autant constituer une preuve fiable. Aujourd'hui, des outils permettent de fabriquer en quelques secondes de faux tweets, publications Facebook ou conversations WhatsApp tres realistes. Dans cette rubrique « education numerique », on fait le point sur les bons reflexes pour verifier une capture d'ecran, retrouver sa source originale et eviter de partager une fausse information.

items.title: BTS et HND 2026 : le MINESUP publie des taux de réussite en hausse, loin des 14% annoncés
items.description: © DR Le ministre d’État, ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur a rendu publics le 19 août 2026 les résultats officiels du BTS et du HND 2026. Ces résultats démentent le taux de réussite de 14% diffusé en début de semaine. Le taux national officiel s’établit à 45,50% pour le BTS et 54,79% pour le HND. Fin de la polémique. Le MINESUP a officiellement publié les résultats des examens nationaux du Brevet de Technicien Supérieur et du Higher National Diploma, session 2026. Des résultats en net décalage avec les informations erronées qui circulaient en début de semaine et faisaient état d’un taux de réussite de 14% sur le plan national. Selon les chiffres validés par le Ministère, 24 774 candidats étaient inscrits au BTS. Le taux de réussite est de 45,50%. Pour le HND, 19 534 candidats se sont présentés. Le taux de réussite atteint 54,79%. Le Ministre d’État, Ministre de l’Enseignement Supérieur, Chancelier des Ordres Académiques, invite la communauté universitaire nationale à se référer uniquement aux données officielles du MINESUP. Il salue par ailleurs la mobilisation des établissements, des encadreurs et des candidats pour cette session. Les délibérations sont disponibles dans les établissements et sur les canaux officiels du Ministère. Cet article BTS et HND 2026 : le MINESUP publie des taux de réussite en hausse, loin des 14% annoncés est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .
